summary: Preserve degraded run bounds across later receipts and retire replay fences after successful full repair.

replay.detail: Canonical claim folding is unchanged; failed run folds remain excluded until authorized full repair.

schema.detail: Persist local keyed degraded-run-root membership in existing meta rows. This branch also adds naming expression indexes, the degraded-subject partial index, generation triggers, naming scope keys, discovery watermark/fence rows and deferred-replay rows.

rules.detail: Later ordinary claims cannot enqueue or directly rebuild an already-degraded run tree. Tree and part rebuild entrypoints fail closed before hydration; a failed part conservatively excludes its owning root.

compatibility.detail: Downgrade to pre-#6330 main / r5 df4bb3dc is not safety-preserving: storage version remains 20, so its supported-version check does not refuse this store. Unknown projection_health aggregate/error strings are accepted; old status lists non-healthy rows (up to 50) and doctor warns using their count/first message, while healthy fence/discovery rows are not listed. The old projector ignores operation-conflict fence health rows, operation-conflict-run:* membership, naming scope-membership meta keys, discovery watermarks and deferred-replay enforcement; these rows do not cause a schema/startup rejection. Its full replay updates graph health but does not retire these new rows/keys. Old reads/rebuilds therefore lack the new scoped fail-closed and bounded-writer protections: the #9101 freeze class is possible again. New naming from/to expression indexes and the degraded-subject partial index remain valid, SQLite-maintained indexes, not safety guards; their maintenance adds work to matching old-binary writes. The six generation triggers still execute: they reference only existing claims, checkpoint_claims, projection_health and meta columns, with no new function/schema dependency. Claims inserts add a keyed watermark predicate; restored-prefix inserts, claim id/body/store_index updates/deletes and checkpoint mutations additionally update one generation meta row. Thus old writes incur extra work; its latency/throughput impact and an actual old-binary reopen/downgrade cycle are NOT VERIFIED. No wire format changes.

manual.detail: After downgrading and re-upgrading, run fractal replication replay --confirm in a planned window before treating retained degraded state as repaired. Downgrade restores the old unprotected behavior, not the new writer-hold guarantee.

recovery.detail: Re-upgrade retains stale run exclusions and replay-fence/deferred health rows conservatively until successful authorized full repair; old-binary repair does not clear them. Naming startup independently rebuilds from current claims and clears its own naming marker/scope keys. On the next projection pass, discovery scans old-binary appends beyond its saved watermark; retained generation triggers invalidate checkpoint/restored-prefix changes and force rediscovery from zero. Rediscovery restores replay-fence evidence, not retroactive bounded subject repair of work already projected by the old binary. Do not assume downgrade-era projections/markers are automatically reconciled: explicit full replay is the recovery boundary. Successful new-binary full repair atomically clears run exclusions, deferred rows and replay-fence evidence and advances discovery to the repaired store index/source generation; canonical operation conflicts remain recorded.

downtime.detail: No additional index build or deployment downtime is introduced by this correction.
